identity.name: Swaccho Khan
identity.headline: AI Programmer & Agency Founder in Dhaka
identity.tagline: I build with code, learn machines, and ship the web.
identity.positioning: I'm a computer science undergraduate in Dhaka who lives in the terminal. My days go into learning AI and machine learning properly — from the maths up — and into running Websthan, the agency I founded, where I lead the tech team, set the business strategy and look after clients. Everything I do comes back to the same instinct: take a thing apart, understand it, then build it better.
identity.shortBio: Computer Science undergraduate based in Dhaka, Bangladesh. I write code, study machine learning, and run Websthan — a web design and digital marketing agency where I lead the tech team and handle clients.
identity.availability: Open to internships, freelance builds & collaboration

focus.title: AI & Machine Learning
focus.summary: The centre of everything I'm doing right now. I'm working through machine learning from first principles — linear algebra and statistics underneath, Python and the modern ML stack on top — so that I understand models rather than just call them.
points: Python as a first-class ML language: data handling, vectorised maths, experiment loops
Neural network fundamentals — how gradients, layers and loss functions actually behave
Building with LLM APIs and agent tooling, not just prompting them
Turning notebooks into real, deployed, useful software

focus.title: Websthan
focus.summary: The web design and digital marketing agency I founded and run from Dhaka. I lead the tech team, set the business strategy, and stay the point of contact for our clients — so the work has to be right technically and commercially.
points: Lead and manage the tech team — delegation, code standards, delivery
Set business strategy: positioning, pricing, which work we take on
Own client relationships end to end, from first brief to long after launch
Still build: front-end engineering, deployment, SEO and performance

focus.title: Web Development
focus.summary: Where my programming actually began. I've been building websites since long before they paid — blogs, brand sites, experiments and this one.
points: HTML, CSS, JavaScript — written by hand, not generated
Node.js services with real security posture
Motion, 3D and interaction as part of the engineering, not decoration

focus.title: Cybersecurity
focus.summary: A serious side interest. I want the things I build to be defensible, so I read about attack surfaces, web vulnerabilities and hardening — then apply it.
points: Web security fundamentals: CSRF, XSS, CSP, injection, session handling
Defensive engineering habits baked into every project I ship

chapters.title: The Boy and the Machine
chapters.subtitle: Sirajganj, Bangladesh
body: It started the way it starts for a lot of people: a computer, and games I wasn't supposed to be playing. Then the internet arrived properly, and the machine stopped being a toy and became a door.

I was an active, loud child everywhere except in one place — with a book. Reading alone did something to me that nothing else did. It handed me other people's perspectives and quietly built the way I think.
chapters.bridge: The door opened onto a question: what could I actually make with this thing?

chapters.title: Frames and Voice
chapters.subtitle: Video editing · YouTube · a former life
body: The answer, for a while, was video. Editing was the first skill I taught myself off the internet, and it turned into freelance work and then a YouTube channel that changed more than I expected.

It taught me to write a script, hold an audience and say a thing clearly. I don't do it any more — the channel and the edits are an archive now — but somewhere in all that timeline-scrubbing I noticed the software was more interesting to me than the footage.
chapters.bridge: So I put the timeline down and picked up a syllabus.

chapters.title: The School Years
chapters.subtitle: Jewel's Oxford International School & College
body: Twelve years at one school, ending with O-Levels that went well. I was vice-president of the basketball club, volunteered for every school function I could find, and won a fair share of school tournaments along the way.

Then I went back to the same school on the other side of the desk — teaching physics and chemistry, writing lesson plans and learning the thing that has stuck with me longest: you don't really understand something until you have to explain it.
chapters.bridge: Explaining things well turned out to be portable. So did leaving home.

chapters.title: A New Country
chapters.subtitle: SEGi University, Kota Damansara, Malaysia
body: I moved abroad for a Foundation in Science and finished my last semester on a 3.68 CGPA. Physics, chemistry, mathematics, computing — and a much harder syllabus in living alone in a country that wasn't mine.

I joined the Student Representative Council, campaigned in the 2024 presidential election, helped run the university orientation, volunteered on donation drives and tree-planting, and coordinated the Career to Campus fair. I also worked evening shifts to pay for it. It was a full year.
chapters.bridge: A full year, and still not enough. I wanted something that was mine.

chapters.title: The Ledger
chapters.subtitle: Fesco — a cosmetics e-commerce, Malaysia
body: So alongside the studying in Malaysia I started my own small e-commerce selling cosmetic products. I ran all of it myself: sourcing, marketing, sales, customer messages, the lot.

It taught me the unglamorous half of building things — setting a goal, measuring whether you actually hit it, and making the next decision from data rather than from hope. When the foundation programme ended I closed it down and flew home.
chapters.bridge: Home in Bangladesh, with a year of hard lessons and nothing yet to spend them on.

chapters.title: Words on the Page
chapters.subtitle: Medium · a few articles, and counting
body: Reading eventually turned into writing. I've published a handful of articles on Medium so far — I'm a beginner at this and I'd rather say so than pretend otherwise.
But it's already the sharpest thinking tool I own. If I can't write an idea down clearly, I've found I don't understand it yet. That test has saved me more times in code than it has in prose.
chapters.bridge: And what I most wanted to explain clearly was the thing I was building.

chapters.title: Websthan
chapters.subtitle: websthan.online · an agency in Dhaka
body: Websthan is the agency I founded in Dhaka: web design and digital marketing. It stopped being a one-man operation quickly — now I lead the tech team, decide the business strategy, and stay the person clients actually talk to.

In the same stretch I started teaching IELTS at Delta Academy and was named their Best Mentor. Running a team, keeping a client happy and teaching a class turn out to use the same muscle: understand the person in front of you, then deliver.
chapters.bridge: Delivering well got easier. Then I found the problem I actually wanted to spend years on.

chapters.title: Machines That Learn
chapters.subtitle: BSc Computer Science & Engineering, UCSI University — Bangladesh campus
body: I'm now reading Computer Science & Engineering, and my focus has narrowed to one thing: artificial intelligence and machine learning. Not as a buzzword — as mathematics I want to actually hold in my head.

Python, the fundamentals of neural networks, the linear algebra and statistics underneath them, and the engineering discipline to turn a working notebook into something people can use. Cybersecurity sits next to it as the discipline that keeps what I build honest.
chapters.bridge: Which brings the whole thing up to today.

chapters.title: The Next Page
chapters.subtitle: Still being written
body: Every chapter here was a skill I picked up because I was curious, and every one of them fed the next. Editing taught me patience, YouTube taught me to communicate, business taught me to measure, teaching taught me to explain, writing taught me to think.

All of it now points at code. I want to build AI systems that are genuinely useful, keep Websthan growing, and keep leaving a trail of things I made. If you have something worth building, the last chapter of this book is a contact form.

timeline.title: BSc Computer Science & Engineering
timeline.detail: Reading CSE at UCSI's Bangladesh campus, with a self-directed focus on artificial intelligence and machine learning. Building fluency across Python, Java and C++, algorithm design and systems thinking.

timeline.title: Founder & Tech Lead
timeline.detail: Founded and run a web design and digital marketing agency in Dhaka. Manage the team, set business strategy, lead technical delivery and own client relationships — while still building on the front end.

timeline.title: IELTS Instructor
timeline.detail: Teach IELTS Academic across Listening, Reading, Writing and Speaking. Build lesson plans and practice material, coach exam strategy and academic writing.

timeline.title: Moved back to Bangladesh
timeline.detail: Finished the Foundation in Science, closed Fesco and came home. Everything since — Websthan, teaching, and the CSE degree — has been built from Bangladesh.

timeline.title: Career to Campus — Organising Team
timeline.detail: Coordinated the university career fair: event logistics, guiding students and employers, and keeping communication running between both sides.

timeline.title: Community Service Volunteer
timeline.detail: Charity events and donation drives, campus orientation support for new international students, and environmental campaigns including tree planting and recycling.

timeline.title: Representative Council — Presidential Election
timeline.detail: Campaigned in the 2024 SEGi Representative Council presidential election — engaging students, supporting candidates and pushing student representation.

timeline.title: Founder
timeline.detail: Started and ran a small cosmetics e-commerce solo while studying in Malaysia: sourcing, marketing, sales and operations. Learned goal-setting, measurement and data-driven decisions. Wound it down at the end of the foundation programme.

timeline.title: Sales Associate (Part-time)
timeline.detail: Evening shifts alongside full-time study — customer service, register operations, inventory monitoring and store standards.

timeline.title: Foundation in Science
timeline.detail: Physics, chemistry, mathematics, computer science and public speaking, studied in Malaysia. Finished the final semester on a 3.68 CGPA while serving on the Student Representative Council, then returned to Bangladesh.

timeline.title: Science Teacher
timeline.detail: Taught physics and chemistry to O-Level students. Wrote full lesson plans against the O-Level syllabus, set and marked examinations and coursework.

timeline.title: School & O-Levels
timeline.detail: Twelve years at the same school, finishing with strong Cambridge O-Level results. Vice-president of the basketball club and a fixture at every school function.

hobbies.name: Coding
hobbies.detail: Hobby and profession at once. Most of my side projects start at 1am with no plan whatsoever.

hobbies.name: Reading
hobbies.detail: The oldest habit I have. Fiction, non-fiction, whatever rearranges how I see a thing.

hobbies.name: Writing
hobbies.detail: Still new at it — a few articles on Medium so far. It's how I find out whether I actually understand something.

hobbies.name: Chess
hobbies.detail: Slow, quiet, and the only game where I can feel myself getting better at thinking.

hobbies.name: Photography
hobbies.detail: A leftover from the editing years — I still frame things before I look at them.

hobbies.name: YouTube & video editing
hobbies.detail: Years of freelance editing and a YouTube channel, back before code took over. I've stopped making them, but the channel and the reel are still up.

writing.note: I'm new to writing publicly — a few articles on Medium so far, on technology, learning, and whatever I've been thinking about too hard. More on the way.
